$comment: What 'the index works' means, in a file rather than in someone's memory. `bbgraph.py selftest` runs it and exits non-zero on any mismatch. Expectations are about the leading MODULE for code questions, because that is the file an agent opens. When a source change legitimately moves an answer, update the expectation in the same commit and say why -- an unexplained edit here is how a ranking bug gets ratified.

queries.note: Regression guard for structural rank deciding rather than ordering. `protocol` is reached by 28 of 33 modules; with an unconditional load-bearing multiplier it won this query outright, which is the download-count failure the method exists to avoid.
None of these three words is a module name; this passes on module doc-comment vocabulary.
Compound-name lookup. Returned `presentation` while a name match required the whole underscored string to appear as one query token.
Not history_store: the store is the persistence layer, the history is the object.

no_match.note: Must return nothing rather than dress a guess as a ranking.

confidence.note: Right answer, low confidence, and that is correct. No subsystem matched this wording, so the ranking is term overlap. Weak-but-right and weak-and-wrong are not separable here, and answering nonsense confidently is the worse failure.
Out of scope. One token lands on host heap metrics; a partial match is not confidence in the query.

$counts_comment: schemas counts PROTOCOL SURFACE only. 23 further schema strings are declared inside a #[cfg(test)] mod and are fixtures; counting them reported 81/50, overstating both the surface and the gap. The boundary is the mod, not the attribute: keying on the first #[cfg(test)] line demoted history.rs GENESIS_SCHEMA and RECEIPT_SCHEMA, both pub, because two test-only use lines sit above them. `bitblock/test-object/v1` is the clearest case -- frame.rs and storage.rs each coined it independently in their own tests, and it had been fusing them into a shared subsystem. schemas_vectored moved 42 -> 44 when journal/rejected-tail/v1 and storage-record/envelope/v1 gained independent Python suites; they were the only two protocol objects with no vector and no literal tag assertion. It moved 44 -> 51 when render_policy_vectors.py, frame_chain_vectors.py, display_receipt_v1_vectors.py and composite_frame_input_vectors.py closed the seven core-crate objects below. Six of the seven already had literal tag assertions in Rust and no second implementation, so those literals were a program agreeing with itself; every one of them reproduced from the Python side unchanged. It then moved again for the research-crate objects, two of them picked up transitively: the headless replay-rules policy names the renderer profile and the crosshair overlay by digest, so reconstructing the rules payload meant reconstructing both from their own constants. The count below is re-derived from the index rather than summed from the two branches, because the transitive pair would be double counted.

structure.note: The most load-bearing module in the workspace. Gained one dependent when the crate split introduced src/lib.rs as a facade that re-exports it -- a re-export is a real edge. Gained another (30 -> 31) when commit_r1 joined crates/research, (31 -> 32) when local_bounds joined, and (32 -> 34) when octree_commit and scale_assay joined.

Two thirds of the crate reaches the world model, most of it through frame and render rather than directly. Gained one dependent (22 -> 23) when commit_r1 imported World for root hashing, (23 -> 24) through local_bounds transitively reaching history_store/storage, and (24 -> 26) when octree_commit and scale_assay joined.
A leaf: research-only, nothing depends on it. Safe to change in isolation.

schemas.note: The canonical framebuffer domain. An independent Python reconstruction must keep agreeing with it.
v3 adds the accepted-action ledger. ACCOUNT-1: three control actions applied outside the edit fold used to leave no trace in the tick, so a tick that consumed them hashed identically to an idle one.

Was recorded as uncovered on purpose, with a standing instruction to flip it in the same commit as its vectors. tools/render_policy_vectors.py now rebuilds the 16-byte payload from the declared constants and reproduces the literal render.rs already asserted.
Was one of the two objects nothing independently checked. The vector varies offset and suffix separately, because the tag exists to bind both.

The outermost envelope. Its vector rebuilds magic, version, declared length, parent flag, kind name, object digest, schema and payload, and both sides assert the same literal record tag over the `on 0 0 0` edit from edit_vectors.py.

render_policy_vectors.py rebuilds the 106-byte profile from the declared constants. Three of its twelve palette slots hold the same word, so equality of a colour proves nothing about position; the vector moves one slot at a time and requires 25 distinct tags.

The policy-plus-optional-payload object a FrameInput actually binds. An absent payload pads with 32 zero bytes, so None and Some(all-zero digest) differ only in the present marker; the vector pins that both ways.

frame_chain_vectors.py rebuilds the 184-byte payload and composes the renderer profile and crosshair overlay from render_policy_vectors.py. The ten camera lanes are hashed as bits, so swapping +0.0 and -0.0 must move the tag.
The same suite varies parent presence, parent identity, source tick, input and frame independently. An absent parent and a genuinely all-zero parent differ only in one marker byte.

display_receipt_v1_vectors.py pins a matching capture, a mismatching capture and an attempt refused before readback. All three are the same schema and the same 312 bytes; only the fact lanes separate them. Its 175-byte capture-facts block is shared with display_receipt_v2_vectors.py.

The only one of the seven with no literal tag anywhere before this commit -- it hashes under kind `frame-input`, the same kind as the inner game input it contains, so a grep for its kind found the game input instead. composite_frame_input_vectors.py composes all four nested digests from suites that already derive them.

A nullary policy: the payload is empty, so the schema string is the entire hashed claim. tools/history_mode_vectors.py re-encodes that same empty payload under neighbouring schemas to show the domain wrapper is what separates them, and sequential.rs asserts the tag.

Binds exactly the iterated-function policy digest, which is what stops a transcript admitted under one recurrence being read under another. The vector moves the function by one bit and requires the mode to move with it.

Two fields, and the second is the point: the declared artifact length is inside the hashed domain, so a stream a reader stopped early on cannot be relabelled as the complete build. The vector holds each field while moving the other, and carries a big-endian control the length lane would fail.

The heaviest of the seven: the payload frames whole nested TickOutcome and FrameReceiptV2 objects, so the vector had to reconstruct both codecs before it could reconstruct this one. Its decisive case is two ledgers ending on the same selected frame that differ only by one retained idle tick nothing presented -- exactly what a head-only commitment cannot separate. Its nested genesis outcome is byte-identical to the genesis-idle payload tick_outcome_vectors.py already pins, so the two suites cross-check each other.

One of three main.rs policies whose literals were pinned before anything independent derived them -- the Rust test and the Rust encoder agreeing, which a consistent change to both would have passed. The reconstruction is complete: World::new() is one bedrock coordinate, and Camera::for_observer_spawn() has yaw wrapping to exactly 0.0 and position exactly (0, 0, -1), so nothing here needed a digest copied out of the implementation. The field-of-view lane is the sharp edge: `math.pi / 3` is one ulp from core::f64::consts::FRAC_PI_3 and that single bit moves the tag, so the tool spells the constant and carries a one-ulp control.

Names the renderer profile, crosshair overlay and composite policy by digest, so deriving it meant deriving all three. Renderer and crosshair come from their own declared constants; the composite chains through the sidebar raster policy, whose authored metric-binding table is read from sidebar.rs and checked against registry.tsv rather than transcribed.
Pure declared limits: eight u64 count lanes then eight u128 work lanes. The width difference is load-bearing, so the vector re-encodes the second half as u64 and requires the tag to move.
Candidate B 192-level Sparse Merkle Tree world root commitment. tools/commit_r1_vectors.py independently rebuilds empty root and bedrock world.
Candidate A fixed-key binary Merkle Patricia Trie world root commitment. tools/commit_r1_vectors.py independently rebuilds empty root and bedrock world.
LOCAL-BOUNDS-1 canonical storage and recovery limits profile. tools/local_bounds_vectors.py independently derives payload and tag.

$reuse_comment: Compression targets, so a refactor that claims to remove duplication has to move these. Production and test scope are separate on purpose: the first pass measured them together and named presentation_output <-> _v2 the biggest target in the crate, when most of that pair's overlap is test fixtures. Numbers here are the measured baseline, not a goal - the tree turned out to be far less duplicated than the first scan suggested. unreferenced_pub_items went 4 -> 3 when examples/render_time_probe.rs started calling Camera::set_observation_anchor, which had been dead. Writing a probe that needed it is what made it live.
